attributes.residual: THIS KEEP WAS BANKED AT A FUZZY REGRESSION and the next lane must know it: `probe.py --arbitrate` printed BANKED real 229 fuzzy 94.4425% against CURRENT real 210 fuzzy 93.2553%, DELTA real -19 fuzzy -1.1872 (= -0.0010 PROJECT-WEIGHTED), and its ARBITER line said REVERT. It was banked deliberately with `--rebase-best --accept-fuzzy-loss`, so every later probe on this function is anchored on a state the project scores worse, and any negative must be re-derived from commit fbfdd3e95. The reasoning, stated so it can be overturned: fuzzy was the ONLY indicator that fell. The instruction count moved 232 -> 233 of 235, the ours-only half of the opcode multiset emptied (`-1 lwzu` -> none), the same-opcode IMMEDIATE rows went 1 -> 0, the branch-target drift rows went 22 -> 16, savedregs role mismatches went 4 -> 3 with r24 becoming an exact match in both streams, and the DATA delta was net +0 B. The fuzzy arbiter law is scoped to EQUAL-COUNT opcode respells and this was not one; count parity is categorical and objdiff's fuzzy is an alignment measure over a stream still two instructions short, which is where the 1.19 comes from. If the remaining gap closes to T235/O235 and fuzzy does NOT recover past 94.4425%, this judgement was wrong and the keep should be revisited. WHAT REMAINS at real 210: (a) the two-instruction gap at @0x204 -- see this record's hypothesis; (b) a count-neutral schedule cluster at @0x174-0x190 where both streams emit the same eight instructions and we hoist the second `rlwinm` four bytes earlier; (c) a save-set permutation in the printf loop at 0x28c-0x330 where the direction INVERTS -- the target caches an address (`@0x31c add r23,r30,r29`) where we hold a loop constant (`@0x328 li r23,8`), which is the opposite of the defect closed here and should be worked as its own mechanism, not as more of this one; (d) 16 branch-target rows that are pure downstream drift from (a) and will close with it.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/game/controls.c PlayerControls 0x1e0:0x210 --diff` after that edit. If `@0x204 lwz r4,32(r3)` still reads off a register defined before the `ble` -- i.e. the else still inherits a base -- the condition side is not the discriminant either, and the two-instruction gap should be reclassified as allocator rematerialisation policy rather than anything source-reachable.
hypothesis.count_consequence: The target is +2 on us (235 vs 233), so the cure must ADD exactly the `slwi` and the `add` and reach T235/O235. A form that changes the count in the other direction, or that adds them while losing an instruction elsewhere, has hit a different mechanism and is not an F3 result.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- every register, offset and instruction quoted above is read from `fnasm --diff` and from a two-stream register census of r8/r9 (target) against r7 (ours) over 0x140:0x300, and is accurate. What is NOT screened is whether hoisting the magnitude read costs a local: the frame is 88/88 exactly today, and this run measured on pbFrameMode that a declared s32 is worth 4 bytes of nominal local area, so a new local may widen the frame and would have to reuse an existing declaration to stay neutral.
hypothesis.statement: The remaining two-instruction gap is the SAME mechanism this run closed at the first site, and it should yield to the same lever applied on the CONDITION side rather than the else side. Measured: the target keeps `pad` itself in r8 (`@0x148 lwz r8,56(r3)`, still live at `@0x204 slwi r0,r8,2`) and rematerialises `pad*4`, while ours lets `pad` die at `@0x164 slwi r7,r3,2` and keeps only `r30 + pad*4`, so the address computed at `@0x1e4 add r3,r30,r7` for the condition `lbl_80240F30[pad] > 0.5` is still live in the else and gets reused by `@0x204 lwz r4,32(r3)`. The proof that this is a CSE-across-the-branch and not a scaling question is the SIBLING if/else 8 lines earlier (lines 1470-1476): it has the identical shape but its else indexes by `[dy][dx]` instead of `[pad]`, shares no base, and matches the target exactly. The untried handle is therefore to stop the CONDITION from producing a base the else can inherit -- read the right-stick magnitude into a local before the `scheme == 2` test and branch on the local, so the only `pad`-indexed address inside the if is the else's own.
